Since, $2^{6 x}-3\left(2^{3 x+2}\right)+32=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow\left(2^{3 x}\right)^2-12\left(2^{3 x}\right)+32=0 \\ & \text { Let } y=2^{3 x} \\ & \therefore y^2-12 y+32=0 \\ & (y-4)(y-8)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow y=4 \quad \text { or, } y=8 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^{3 x}=4 \quad \text { or, } 2^{3 x}=8 \\ & \Rightarrow 2^{3 x}=22 \quad \text { or, } 2^{3 x}=23\end{aligned}\Rightarrow x=\frac{2}{3} \quad$ or, $x=1$
Hence, $\alpha=1 \& \beta=\frac{2}{3}$
Then, $2 \alpha+3 \beta=2 \times 1+3 \times \frac{2}{3}=4$

questions.solution:
Since, $\alpha_1, \alpha_2 \& \alpha_3$ are the roots of $x^3+3 x+2=0$.
$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3=0 \\ & \alpha_1 \alpha_2+\alpha_2 \alpha_3+\alpha_3 \alpha_1=3 \\ & \alpha_1 \alpha_2 \alpha_3=-2\end{aligned}$
Now, $\alpha_1^5+\alpha_2^5+\alpha_3^5=\alpha_1^3 \cdot \alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^3 \alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^3 \alpha_3^2\begin{aligned} & =\left(-3 \alpha_1-2\right) \cdot \alpha_1^2+\left(-3 \alpha_2-2\right) \alpha_2^2+\left(-3 \alpha_3-2\right) \alpha_3^2 \\ & =-3 \alpha_1^3-2 \alpha_1^2-3 \alpha_2^3-2 \alpha_2^2-3 \alpha_3^3-2 \alpha_3^2 \\ & =-\left(-3 \alpha_1-2\right)-3\left(3 \alpha_2-2\right)-3\left(3 \alpha_3-2\right)-2\left(\alpha_1^2+\alpha_2^2+\alpha_3^2\right) \\ & =9\left(\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\right)-2\left[\left(\alpha_1+\alpha_2+\alpha_3\right)^2-2\left(\alpha_2 \alpha_1+\alpha_2 \alpha_3\right.\right. \\ & =9 \times 0-2\left[0^2-2 \times(3)\right]+18 \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha_1^5+\alpha_2^5+\alpha_3^5=30\end{aligned}$

$\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2-2 x+2}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2+2 x+2}\Rightarrow \frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}=\frac{(A x+B)\left(x^2+2 x+2\right)+(C x+D)\left(x^2-2 x+2\right)}{\left(x^2+2\right)^2-(2 x)^2}\Rightarrow x^2+1=(A+C) x^3+(2 A+B-2 C+D) x^2+(2 A+2 B+2 C-2 D) x+(2 B+2 D)$
On comparing both sides,
$A+C=0 \Rightarrow A=-C, 2 B+2 D=1$
and $2 A+B-2 C+D=1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2(A-C)+B+D=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 4 A+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 4 A=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad A=\frac{1}{8} \text { and } C=-\frac{1}{8}\end{aligned}$
Now, $2 A+2 B+2 C-2 D=0\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad 2(A+C)+2(B-D)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad B=D \\ & \text { and } 2 B+2 D=1\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad 4 B=1 \Rightarrow B=D=\frac{1}{4}$
Now, $3 A+2 B+3 C=2 B \quad[\because 3 A+3 C=0]=2 D$
